picks.file: Prospectus Templi Cathedralis quod est Basileae, nec non Pontis Rhenum transeuntis, admodum delectabilis ; Campus Divi Petri qui est Basileae - M. Merian fecit - btv1b53238827f (1 of 2).jpg
picks.what: The Minster and the Rhine bridge, engraving in Merian’s Topographia Helvetiae
picks.why: classic view from the Minster terrace up the Rhine to the Middle Bridge and Kleinbasel; trimmed to the top plate (St. Peter’s Square below)

picks.what: The town hall on the Marktplatz, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: the red Rathaus, the city’s best-known building; color, high resolution, landscape format

picks.file: ETH-BIB-Basel, Altstadt, Zentrum, Münster aus 300 m-Inlandflüge-LBS MH01-001422.tif
picks.what: The old town and the Minster from 300 m, aerial photograph (ETH Library, Zurich)
picks.why: sharp oblique aerial of the old town with the Minster and the Middle Bridge on the Rhine

picks.what: The Minster above the Rhine with the Münster ferry, photograph
picks.why: the signature Basel view: Minster on its terrace, Rhine and reaction ferry; color, wide format

gaps: P0: the Nuremberg Chronicle woodcut exists only as two-page spreads with the gutter through the view (#1–#3). P2, P3: no views (the many ‘Merian’ hits #12–#17 are portraits of Basel’s Merian family).
notes: #11 date: BnF gives only ‘17th century’; the plate is Merian’s (died 1650) and matches the Basel plates of Topographia Helvetiae, 1642 — change if a different edition is confirmed. #21 date: LOC’s ‘1890’ is impossible, because the Rathaus tower shown was built 1900–1904, so ‘about 1905’ is used. P1 alternatives are perspective plans: Braun and Hogenberg vol. 2 (#5 is a book photo with the gutter through the plan; #9 black and white) and Merian’s 1642 plan (#6). P4 alternative: Spalentor (#20, 1890s), portrait format.
